## load libraries    
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(rio)
library(janitor)
library(ggplot2)

```

## loading data 
```{r}
asvab_data <- read_excel("asvab_data_2020-2024.xlsx")
```


## clean heading names 
```{r}
asvab_data <- asvab_data|> 
  clean_names()
```

## clean data 

```{r}
asvab_clean <- asvab_data %>%
  # Remove rows with all NA values (optional)
  filter(if_any(everything(), ~ !is.na(.))) %>%
  
  # Trim whitespace from character columns
  mutate(across(where(is.character), str_trim)) %>%
  
  # Convert empty strings to NA
  mutate(across(where(is.character), ~ na_if(., ""))) %>%
  
  # Handle known inconsistent values (e.g., "N/A", "NA", "Unknown")
  mutate(across(where(is.character), ~ na_if(., "N/A"))) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.character), ~ na_if(., "Unknown"))) 
  
```




## summarizing the data 
  
  ### race distribution 

```{r}
race_counts <- asvab_clean |> 
  separate_rows(race, sep = ",\\s*") |>   # splits by comma and optional space
  count(race, sort = TRUE) 

print(race_counts)
```

 ### gender distribution 
```{r}
gender_count <- asvab_clean |> 
  count(sex, sort = TRUE) |> 
  print()

```


  ### age distribution 
  
```{r}
age_count <- asvab_clean |> 
  count(age, sort=TRUE) |> 
  print()
```
  ### producing age ranges 
```{r}
asvab_clean <- asvab_clean %>%
  mutate(age_range = cut(
    age,
    breaks = c(17, 24, 34, 44, 54, 64, Inf),  # customize as needed
    labels = c("16–24", "25–34", "35–44", "45–54", "55–64", "65+"),
    right = TRUE,   # include the upper bound (e.g., 24 is part of 18–24)
    include.lowest = TRUE
  ))


```

## age range 
```{r}
asvab_clean |> 
  count(age_range)
```

### Latest Schooling By Race 
```{r}
latest_schooling_by_race <- asvab_clean |> 
  group_by(race, latest_school_type) |> 
  summarise(count = n(), .groups = "drop")

print(latest_schooling_by_race)
```

```{r}
ggplot(latest_schooling_by_race, aes(x = race, y = count)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2c7fb8") +
  facet_wrap(~ latest_school_type, scales = "free_y") +  # each school type gets its own plot
  labs(title = "Race Count per School Type",
       x = "Race",
       y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, size = 7),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 10),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5)
  )

```

```{r}
latest_schooling_by_gender <- asvab_clean |>

print(latest_schooling_by_gender) 
  
```

### General Science Asvab scores by race 
```{r}

general_science_scores <- asvab_clean |> 
    group_by(race, asvab_gs) |> 
  summarise(count = n(), .groups = "drop")

print(general_science_scores) 


```


### trying to make graphics for the genearl science asvab scores 
```{r}
ggplot(general_science_scores, aes(x = asvab_gs, y = count)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#3182bd") +
  facet_wrap(~ race, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "ASVAB GS Scores by Race",
       x = "ASVAB GS Score",
       y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, size = 6),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10)
  )

```

```{r}
ggplot(asvab_clean, aes(x = asvab_gs)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 2, fill = "#3182bd", color = "white") +
  facet_wrap(~ race, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of ASVAB General Science Scores by Race",
    x = "ASVAB GS Score",
    y = "Count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(size = 8),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 6)
  )
```

### fix this 
```{r}
ggplot(general_science_scores, aes(x = asvab_gs, y = count, fill = race)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of ASVAB GS Scores by Race",
    x = "ASVAB GS Score",
    y = "Count",
    fill = "Race"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )
```
